text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Swedish medical and technical gas group AGA might move its head office abroad. Telecoms group Ericsson is also considering a move for tax reasons and several companies would welcome tax reliefs for key foreign staffers.

- There is currently no majority within the ruling Social Democratic party for Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from the start in 1999, Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said.
- One-third of managers for Sweden's largest listed companies received raises of at least 25 percent in 1996. Hakan Mogren, managing director of Swedish drug company Astra, is the most well-paid.

- The Swedish government think-tank KI, or the Swedish Economic Research Institute, generates the country's most important economic forecasts but they are not very good. The instititute's new director, Svante Oberg, would like to make huge investments in order to increase the precision of the forecasts.

- Telecoms group Ericsson is not the only Swedish firm considering moving its operations abroad. Insurance company SPP is also transfering strategic parts of its business overseas because of an unfavourable tax climate in Sweden.
- Swedish capital fund managers have transfered money abroad recently, resulting in the weakening of the crown in the past half year.
